### `delete_agent`

Hard-destroy an AI agent. Cascades children (executions/conversations/messages/skills/etc) via dependent:destroy. For FKs without dependent: (mcp_sessions, ralph_loops.default_agent_id, team memberships, telemetry, learnings, messages, a2a tasks, etc), if reassign_to_agent_id is given those rows are repointed to it; otherwise they are deleted. Irreversible.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::AgentManagementTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.execute

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | Agent UUID, slug, or name to destroy |
| `reassign_to_agent_id` | string | No | Agent UUID, slug, or name to repoint un-cascaded FKs to. If omitted, those rows are deleted. |

## AI Safety & Autonomy

### `emergency_halt`

Emergency halt ALL AI activity for the account. Cancels running executions, pauses schedules, blocks LLM calls, and demotes all agents to supervised tier.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::KillSwitchTool`
- **Permission**: ai.kill_switch.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `reason` | string | No | Reason for the emergency halt |

### `emergency_resume`

Resume AI activity after an emergency halt. 'full' mode restores agent trust tiers and schedules from pre-halt snapshot. 'minimal' mode only lifts the suspension.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::KillSwitchTool`
- **Permission**: ai.kill_switch.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | No | Resume mode: 'full' (restore snapshot, default) or 'minimal' (lift suspension only) |

## Activity Monitoring

### `get_activity_feed`

Get a unified activity feed of recent missions, conversations, execution events, and errors across the platform

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `hours` | integer | No | Lookback window in hours (default 24, max 168) |
| `limit` | integer | No | Max items per category (default 10, max 50) |

### `get_mission_status`

Get mission status. Without mission_id: all in-progress missions with approval gates. With mission_id: full mission details.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | No | Specific mission ID for full details (omit for overview) |

### `get_notifications`

Get notifications for the current user. Defaults to active+unread (default 10, max 50). Filterable by category, type, source_type, before timestamp, or unread_only=false to include read.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `limit` | integer | No | Max notifications to return (default 10, max 50) |
| `category` | string | No | Filter by category (e.g. ai, system, security) |
| `type` | string | No | Filter by notification type (e.g. autonomy_approval_required, ai_concierge_message) |
| `source_type` | string | No | Filter by metadata.source_type (e.g. system_fleet, system_cve_responder) |
| `before` | string | No | Only return notifications created before this ISO8601 timestamp |
| `unread_only` | boolean | No | Restrict to unread (default true) |

### `dismiss_notification`

Mark a notification as read

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `notification_id` | string | Yes | ID of the notification to dismiss |

### `dismiss_all_notifications`

Dismiss all active notifications permanently (sets dismissed_at). Returns count of dismissed.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `mark_all_notifications_read`

Mark all unread notifications as read (lighter than dismiss — still visible but marked as read). Returns count.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ActivityMonitorTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

Get a lightweight system health snapshot: active counts, approval queues, error rates, and provider status

- **Permission**: ai.agents.read
- **Parameters**: none

## Uncategorized

### `system_assign_storage_owner`

Set the owner of a StorageAssignment. For owner_kind=service_user, supply service_user_username — the platform looks up (or auto-allocates via Identity::UserAllocator) the matching ServiceUser. For operator/nobody/root, only owner_kind is required. Optional shared_group_groupname overrides the default anongid (the owner's primary group) for multi-service write-shared mounts. Triggers an automatic chown task on the storage provider node; the NFS export keeps using the OLD anonuid until the chown completes to avoid EACCES storms on consuming services.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `owner_kind` | string | Yes | service_user | operator | nobody | root |
| `service_user_username` | string | No | Required when owner_kind=service_user |
| `shared_group_groupname` | string | No | Optional override of anongid for shared-write mounts |

### `system_list_storage_assignments_by_owner`

List StorageAssignments filtered by owner_kind, service_user_username, chown_state, or node_instance_id. Use for ops audits like "which assignments still use owner_kind=root?" or "show me every chown that's stuck in failed across the fleet".

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `owner_kind` | string | No | - |
| `service_user_username` | string | No | - |
| `node_instance_id` | string | No | - |
| `chown_state` | string | No | complete | pending | running | failed | manual_required |

### `system_storage_chown_status`

Inspect chown state of a StorageAssignment — current state, previous_uid/gid (if in flight), task id, start/complete timestamps, recorded error.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_storage_chown_retry`

Re-dispatch a failed or manual_required chown. Resets chown_last_error and transitions back to pending — the after_commit dispatch hook then queues a fresh task. Pass force_complete: true as an escape hatch for cases where the operator has manually chowned the files (e.g. on an external NFS provider the platform can't reach) and wants to flip the assignment to complete without re-running.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemStorageOwnerTool`
- **Permission**: system.storage.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `storage_assignment_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `force_complete` | boolean | No | - |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `target_peer_id` | string | No | Sdwan::Peer hosting the backend (mutually exclusive with target_instance_id) |

Fetch a single ACME certificate's non-secret detail (status, issuer, expiry, vault_paths_present). NEVER returns PEMs, private keys, or Vault secret values.

Renew an ACME certificate currently in status=valid. Drives valid → renewing → valid via Acme::CertificateManager.renew!. Returns the reloaded non-secret cert detail on success.

Revoke a non-terminal ACME certificate via Acme::CertificateManager.revoke!. Drives any non-terminal status → revoked. Optionally records a revocation reason.

### `system_acme_create_dns_credential`

Register a new ACME DNS-01 provider credential (Cloudflare, Route53, etc.). The provider API token in `credentials` is handed straight to Vault — NEVER stored on the model, logged, or returned. The result serializes only the public index (name, provider, status).

| `provider` | string | Yes | DNS provider slug (cloudflare|route53|gcloud|digitalocean|hetzner|porkbun|ovh) |
| `credentials` | object | Yes | Provider-specific secret token fields (SENSITIVE — stored in Vault only) |
| `metadata` | object | No | - |

### `system_grant_instance_mcp_tools`

Grant an instance-agent the MCP tool-name glob patterns it may invoke on the platform MCP (default-deny: an instance can call nothing until granted). Patterns match the 'platform.<tool>' name, e.g. 'platform.system_*_read' or 'platform.health'. mode: 'replace' (default) or 'add'. The instance must have announced as a peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `tool_patterns` | array | Yes | - |
| `mode` | string | No | - |

### `system_grant_instance_peer_skills`

A2A: grant an instance-agent the peer skill-name glob patterns it may invoke on OTHER instances via agent-to-agent MCP (default-deny). Patterns match a peer's offered skill name, e.g. 'embed-*' or 'summarize'. mode: 'replace' (default) or 'add'. The instance must have announced as a peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `skill_patterns` | array | Yes | - |
| `mode` | string | No | - |

A2A: list the online, operator-enabled agent peers in the account and the skills they offer (capability discovery). Pass instance_id to discover from a specific caller's perspective (excludes itself). Discovery does not imply call permission — the call is still gated by system_authorize_peer_call.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `instance_id` | string | No | - |

A2A: decide whether a caller instance may invoke a skill on a target instance via agent-to-agent MCP (three-gate, default-deny: caller granted + target online/enabled + target offers skill + same account). Returns { authorized, reason }. Consulted by the on-node A2A transport before relaying a call.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `caller_instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `target_instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `skill` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_launch_agent_fleet`

L3: launch an agent-fleet orchestration mission — dynamically provision a fleet of agent-instances, grant them L2 (platform-MCP) + L2.5 (A2A) capabilities, delegate subtasks (hybrid coordinator + peer sub-delegation), aggregate, and reap. Creates an approval-gated Ai::Mission (mission_type: agent_fleet) bound to the system_agent_fleet template and starts it; the operator approves the review_fleet gate before any instances are provisioned. fleet_spec: { size, source('provision'|'pool'), node_id, provider_region_id, provider_instance_type_id, pool_name, grant_mcp_tools[], grant_peer_skills[], member_skills[], subtasks[{id,skill}], delegation('central'|'a2a'|'hybrid'), reap }.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `fleet_spec` | object | Yes | - |
| `name` | string | No | - |
| `objective` | string | No | - |

### `system_agent_fleet_status`

L3: inspect an agent-fleet mission — returns status, current_phase, error_message, and a summary of the fleet (plan, member/assignment counts, aggregated report, per-member reap actions, reap_incomplete flag).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| `mission_id` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_reap_agent_fleet`

L3: re-run reap for a failed/stuck agent-fleet mission — returns pool members, terminates provisioned members, disables their peers. Safe to retry; reports per-member actions and a reap_incomplete flag when any member fails to terminate. Pass force:true to reap a fleet whose plan disabled reaping.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `force` | boolean | No | Reap even when the fleet plan set reap:false |

### `system_mint_peer_capability_token`

A2A: mint an Ed25519-signed capability token proving caller_instance may invoke `skill` on target_instance via agent-to-agent MCP. GATED on the 4-gate A2A policy (PeerCapabilityService.authorize) — only issued if the call is authorized. The on-node A2A MCP server verifies the token's signature OFFLINE against the advertised public key (no per-call platform round-trip). Short-lived (default 5 min). Returns { envelope, signature, handle, public_key, expires_at, sub, aud, skill, jti }.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `caller_instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `target_instance_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `skill` | string | Yes | - |
| `ttl_seconds` | integer | No | Default 300; clamped to 1..3600 (MAX_TTL_SECONDS) — revocation propagates via the agents' capability_keys pull, so token lifetime is hard-capped |

### `system_list_isolation_tiers`

L0: list the isolation tiers an agent deployment can request (native | gvisor | kata | firecracker | vm) with their Docker runtime / K8s RuntimeClass mapping, isolation strength, overhead, and host requirements. Pass isolation_tier inside a fleet_spec (system_launch_agent_fleet) to select one (default native).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read
- **Parameters**: none

Update a provider — supports name + enabled + config. Config is merge-updated (existing keys preserved unless explicitly nilled). Use this to set host_node_instance_id on a routed-mode QEMU provider, swap the bridge_name, etc.

| `name` | string | No | - |

### `system_create_provider`

Create a substrate provider record (e.g. onboard a new local_qemu/libvirt host). Credentials are NOT accepted here — attach them afterwards via the Vault-backed provider credential flow (provider connections + BYOC credential test); secret material must never transit tool calls.

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|

| `config` | object | No | Non-secret wiring config (e.g. host_node_instance_id, bridge_name) |

Delete a provider record. CASCADES: the provider's regions, connections, instance types, volume types and networks are destroyed with it — decommission instances first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | System::Provider id |

### `system_recycle_pool`

Recycle stale members of a pool: warming members past warming_timeout_seconds become errored, ready members past ready_ttl_seconds become draining. Returns counts of transitions made. Normally the reaper does this every 60s before replenish; this is for impatient operators or for unwedging a pool that's stuck with zombie warming members blocking the deficit calculation.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_search_packages`

Search the synced apt/rpm package catalog. Supports name+description trigram + semantic embedding ranking (mode: lexical|semantic|hybrid, default hybrid). Filters: kind (apt/rpm/dnf), repository_ids[], architectures[] (canonical, cross-kind expanded), sections[], license, provides (capability lookup).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemPackageRepositoryTool`
- **Permission**: system.packages.view

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `q` | string | No | - |
| `mode` | string | No | lexical | semantic | hybrid (default hybrid; blank q forces lexical) |
| `sort` | string | No | relevance | name | updated (default relevance) |
| `repository_id` | string | No | Back-compat: singular form of repository_ids |
| `repository_ids` | array | No | - |
| `kind` | string | No | apt | rpm | dnf |
| `architecture` | string | No | Back-compat: singular form of architectures |
| `architectures` | array | No | Canonical arch names (amd64, arm64) — cross-kind expanded |
| `section` | string | No | Back-compat: singular form of sections |
| `sections` | array | No | - |
| `license` | string | No | - |
| `provides` | string | No | Capability name — finds packages whose name=capability OR provides @> [{name: capability}] |
| `page` | integer | No | - |
| `per_page` | integer | No | - |

### `system_discover_packages`

Intent-based package discovery — describe a capability ('reverse proxy', 'distributed cache') and get ranked packages from accessible repositories. Pure semantic ranking via pgvector cosine distance. Use system_search_packages instead when you already know the package name.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemPackageRepositoryTool`
- **Permission**: system.packages.view

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `intent` | string | Yes | Free-text capability description — what the package should do |
| `repository_ids` | array | No | - |
| `kind` | string | No | apt | rpm | dnf |
| `architectures` | array | No | Canonical arch names — cross-kind expanded |
| `license` | string | No | - |
| `top_k` | integer | No | Max results (1-50, default 10) |

Fetch the exposure breakdown for a CVE — exposed modules + per-module assignment counts, account-scoped via CveExposure → NodeModuleVersion → NodeModule.

### `system_create_cve`

Manually inject a Cve row (typically for embargoed CVEs not yet in NVD, or for drill-mode runbooks). Idempotent via cve_id uniqueness — re-running updates fields. NOTE: Cve table is GLOBAL (not account-scoped) — created CVEs are visible to all accounts. Requires elevated system.fleet.autonomy permission.

- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `summary` | string | No | - |
| `affected_packages` | array | No | [{name: 'openssl', version: '<3.1.4'}, ...] |
| `published_at` | string | No | ISO8601; defaults to now |
| `reference_url` | string | No | - |
| `feed_source` | string | No | nvd|ghsa|manual (default manual) |

Destroy a Cve row + cascade-delete its CveExposures. Used for drill cleanup. Cves are global; deletion affects all accounts. Requires elevated system.fleet.autonomy permission.

Enable or disable a NodeModuleAssignment (per-(node, module) toggle). enabled=true enables the assignment; enabled=false disables it. ### `system_deploy_platform`

Deploy a new Powernode platform. Two execution shapes: (1) call with no `mode` to receive a wizard-card payload describing the form fields the operator should fill in — the chat UI renders this inline; (2) call with full args (mode, name, template_slug, [parent_url, spawn_mode for federated]) to actually provision. Standalone = sovereign platform; federated = peers back with this platform via P6 spawn flow. Federated mode returns a single-use acceptance_token that must be captured immediately.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mode` | string | No | standalone | federated. Omit to receive the wizard payload. |
| `name` | string | No | Display name for the new deployment (required when mode is set). |
| `template_slug` | string | No | NodeTemplate to provision from (defaults to powernode-hub). |
| `parent_url` | string | No | Required for federated mode — reachable URL of THIS platform. |
| `spawn_mode` | string | No | Required for federated mode — one of managed_child, autonomous_peer, cluster_member. |
| `region` | string | No | - |
| `instance_size` | string | No | - |
| `service_role` | string | No | - |
| `public_dns_hostname` | string | No | - |
| `token_ttl_seconds` | integer | No | - |

Register a new ProviderVolume. For NFS, pass transport=nfs + nfs_server + nfs_export_path. For block, pass volume_type_id. The platform records the row; on-node mounting happens at attach time.

### `system_set_default_disk_image_publication`

Promote a published DiskImagePublication as the platform's active disk image — copies its OCI ref + git SHA onto the parent NodePlatform so new instances boot from it. Errors if the publication is not in 'published' state.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `publication_id` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_revert_disk_image`

Roll a NodePlatform's disk image back to a prior publication — restores the target publication's file_object onto the platform (and un-soft-deletes it if the target was retired), then retires the previously-active publication. With publication_id, rolls back to that specific publication; without it, auto-selects the most recent prior publication (the newest retired one, else the newest published one that isn't currently active). Refuses purged publications (FileObject hard-deleted) and publications with no file_object. Wraps System::Executors::DiskImage::RollbackPublication — the same transaction the DiskImagePublicationsController#rollback :proceed path uses.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.nodes.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `platform_id` | string | Yes | System::NodePlatform id to roll back |
| `publication_id` | string | No | Target DiskImagePublication to restore. Omit to auto-select the previous publication. |

### `system_sdwan_propose_federation_peer`

Propose a new federation peer. Status starts at 'proposed'. With generate_token: true (Phase 11b), generates a single-use acceptance token (plaintext returned ONCE) — Account A operator copies it out-of-band to Account B operator who pastes it into system_sdwan_accept_federation_peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `remote_instance_url` | string | Yes | - |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | - |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | - |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | /48|/56|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `generate_token` | boolean | No | When true, generate a single-use acceptance token (Phase 11b token round-trip handshake). Plaintext returned ONCE — not recoverable. |
| `token_ttl_seconds` | integer | No | Token expiry window in seconds (default 7 days) |

### `system_sdwan_accept_federation_peer`

Transition a proposed federation peer to accepted. When the proposing operator generated a single-use acceptance token, pass it as acceptance_token — it is verified (digest match + not expired + single-use) before the transition is allowed. Sets signed_at + audit metadata and (for platform peers) chains into enroll. Returns the updated peer.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `acceptance_token` | string | No | Single-use token from the proposing-account operator (from propose with generate_token: true). Verified against the stored digest; consumed on success. |

### `system_sdwan_update_federation_peer`

Update a federation peer's mutable fields. When `status` is supplied it is gated by the v1 transition matrix (FederationPeer#can_transition_to?) — disallowed transitions return an error. Mirrors the FederationPeersController#update permitted keys.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `status` | string | No | Target status — must be an allowed v1 transition from the current status |
| `remote_instance_url` | string | No | - |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | - |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | - |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | /48|/56|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `signed_at` | string | No | - |
| `expires_at` | string | No | - |
| `metadata` | object | No | - |

### `system_sdwan_federation_compose`

Stand up a federation overlay topology (hub-and-spoke OR full-mesh) across instances. Creates one Sdwan::Network, enrolls each member as a peer (hubs publicly_reachable), and compiles the per-peer WireGuard + FRR route-policy envelope (Sdwan::PeerEnroller + TopologyCompiler + RoutePolicyCompiler). Failures are collected, not short-circuited.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `network_name` | string | Yes | Display name for the new federation Sdwan::Network |
| `topology` | string | Yes | hub_and_spoke | full_mesh |
| `peers` | array | Yes | Member descriptors (1-200). Each: {node_instance_id (required), role: 'hub'|'spoke' (hub_and_spoke only; default spoke), endpoint_host_v6, endpoint_host_v4, endpoint_port, listen_port, lan_subnets: [cidr], bgp_route_reflector_client: bool} |
| `routing_protocol` | string | No | static (default) | ibgp — 'ibgp' enables FRR route-policy distribution |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Plan only — no rows persisted |

### `system_multi_tenant_isolation`

Provision a fully-isolated SDWAN network slice for a single tenant: a dedicated overlay network with its own VRF + isolated iBGP RIB, a non-overlapping /64, default-deny nftables rules scoped to the tenant CIDR, an OVN logical switch, and tenant-CIDR OVN ACLs. SDWAN-native — no k8s NetworkPolicy, no VLAN. Approval-gated.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `tenant_key` | string | Yes | Stable slug-safe tenant identifier within the account (names the network/rules/switch/ACLs) |
| `network_name` | string | No | Display name for the tenant's Sdwan::Network (defaults to 'tenant-<tenant_key>') |
| `tenant_cidr` | string | No | Explicit tenant CIDR; when omitted the auto-allocated /64 is used (recommended) |
| `nb_db_endpoint` | string | No | OVN NB DB endpoint (e.g. tcp:127.0.0.1:6641) — required only when the account has no Sdwan::OvnDeployment yet |
| `sb_db_endpoint` | string | No | OVN SB DB endpoint (e.g. tcp:127.0.0.1:6642) — required only when the account has no Sdwan::OvnDeployment yet |
| `ovn_switch_name` | string | No | Override the OVN logical switch name (defaults to 'ls-tenant-<tenant_key>') |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Plan only — no rows persisted |

### `system_service_discovery_compose`

Make a backend service discoverable across the fleet over the SDWAN overlay — provisions a Virtual IP (auto-advertised via iBGP for in-overlay discovery), publishes a VIP-backed federation service-catalog offering, regenerates local Traefik routes, and OPTIONALLY publishes a public DNS record (A/AAAA/CNAME) for internet-facing names. Approval-gated.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `service_name` | string | Yes | Human-readable catalog display name |
| `service_slug` | string | Yes | Lowercase-alphanumeric-hyphen slug — the catalog's natural key (also names the VIP) |
| `sdwan_network_id` | string | Yes | SDWAN network the VIP lives in |
| `backend_peer_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::Peer hosting the service; seated as the VIP's primary holder (iBGP advertiser) |
| `backend_port` | integer | Yes | Port the backend service listens on (advertised in the catalog offering) |
| `vip_cidr` | string | Yes | Operator-supplied host CIDR for the VIP (a /128 v6 or /32 v4) within the network's /64 |
| `protocol` | string | No | Service protocol advertised in the catalog: https (default) | http | tcp | tls |
| `grant_scopes` | array | No | Default FederationGrant scopes subscribers receive (subset of read, write, admin, migrate). Defaults to ['read'] |
| `grant_ttl_days` | integer | No | Default grant TTL in days (>= 7) |
| `traefik_dynamic_dir` | string | No | Override for the Traefik dynamic-config directory |
| `public_dns` | object | No | INTERNET-FACING name only: { dns_credential_id, record_name, record_type? (A|AAAA|CNAME), record_content?, ttl? }. Omit for overlay-only discovery. |

### `system_sdwan_list_host_bridges`

List HostBridges for the current account. Optionally filter by node_instance_id.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `node_instance_id` | string | No | - |

### `system_sdwan_activate_host_bridge`

Mark a HostBridge as `active` so the topology compiler picks it up. Newly allocated bridges land in `pending`; the resolver only sees active bridges. Use this after create_host_bridge when the agent isn't yet reporting back its applied state.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::HostBridge id |

### `system_sdwan_release_host_bridge`

Release a HostBridge via Sdwan::HostBridgeAllocator.release!. Default `force: false` transitions the bridge to `draining` (preserves the short_id during in-flight tap teardown). Pass `force: true` to mark the bridge `removed` immediately, releasing the short_id back to the pool.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::HostBridge id |
| `force` | boolean | No | When true, skip the draining grace window and mark removed immediately (default false) |

### `system_sdwan_create_ovn_deployment`

Create the per-account OVN control-plane deployment. One OvnDeployment per account (DB-enforced). Endpoints use OVN's standard `tcp:HOST:PORT` / `ssl:HOST:PORT` / `unix:PATH` form (defaults: NB 6641, SB 6642).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `nb_db_endpoint` | string | Yes | OVN Northbound DB endpoint, e.g. tcp:nb.example:6641 |
| `sb_db_endpoint` | string | Yes | OVN Southbound DB endpoint, e.g. tcp:sb.example:6642 |
| `northd_host` | string | No | Hostname (advisory) of the host running ovn-northd |
| `settings` | object | No | Free-form settings hash |

### `system_sdwan_create_ovn_logical_switch`

Create an OVN logical L2 switch under a deployment. Name is unique per deployment, max 63 chars, [letters/digits/_/-/.] only.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `deployment_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `name` | string | Yes | - |
| `cidr` | string | No | Optional subnet CIDR (sets up DHCP on the switch when present) |
| `description` | string | No | - |
| `settings` | object | No | - |

### `system_sdwan_create_ovn_logical_switch_port`

Create an OVN logical switch port. `kind` drives compiler choices: vm | container = host-backed (host_node_instance_id required for proper placement); external = uplink/transit (no host required, gets lsp-set-type localnet by default). MAC is auto-generated (locally-administered `02:` prefix) when blank.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `logical_switch_id` | string | Yes | - |
| `name` | string | Yes | - |
| `kind` | string | Yes | vm | container | external |
| `host_node_instance_id` | string | No | Required for vm/container ports; ignored for external |
| `addresses` | array | No | Array of IPv4/IPv6 strings; appended to the OVN `addresses=` line |
| `mac` | string | No | MAC in `xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx` form; auto-generated when blank |

### `system_sdwan_compile_ovn_plan`

Compile the structured ovn-nbctl command plan for an OvnDeployment via Sdwan::OvnCompiler. Returns the full plan (deployment_id, plan: array of {cmd, args}, compiled_at). The compiler does NOT execute — it returns the plan as data for an executor or operator to replay against the NB DB.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `deployment_id` | string | Yes | - |

### `system_sdwan_create_ipfix_collector`

Create an IPFIX collector for the current account. When an active collector exists, the topology compiler stamps an `ipfix:` block on every ovs-kind HostBridge in the per-host payload. Linux-bridge hosts ignore IPFIX (no native OVS support).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | Operator-chosen label (unique per account) |
| `host` | string | Yes | Hostname or IP literal of the IPFIX collector |
| `port` | integer | No | UDP port (default 4739, the IANA-assigned IPFIX port) |
| `sampling_rate` | integer | No | 1-in-N packet sampling (default 1 = sample every packet) |

### `system_sdwan_list_ipfix_collectors`

List IPFIX collectors for the current account.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `system_sdwan_create_ovn_acl`

Create an OVN ACL (firewall rule) on a logical switch. ACLs operate at the intra-host / logical-network scope (compiled to OVS OpenFlow via OVN's logical-flow translation) — distinct from SDWAN nftables firewall rules which operate at inter-peer scope. Heavyweight-profile only in effect.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `logical_switch_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::OvnLogicalSwitch id this ACL applies to |
| `name` | string | Yes | Operator-chosen name (unique per switch, max 63 chars, [letters/digits/_/-/.] only) |
| `direction` | string | Yes | from-lport (egress from source pod/VM) | to-lport (ingress to destination) |
| `priority` | integer | No | 0-32767, higher first; default 1000. Ties broken by lexicographic match-string order. |
| `match` | string | Yes | OVN match expression, e.g. `ip4.src == 10.0.0.0/8 && tcp.dst == 5432`. Raw OVN syntax — OVN's parser rejects bad values at apply time. |
| `action` | string | Yes | allow | drop | reject | allow-related |

### `system_sdwan_list_ovn_acls`

List OVN ACLs for the current account. Optionally filter by logical_switch_id (per-switch scope) or sdwan_ovn_deployment_id (per-deployment scope). With no filter, returns every active ACL across every switch in every deployment.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `logical_switch_id` | string | No | Restrict to ACLs on this switch |
| `sdwan_ovn_deployment_id` | string | No | Restrict to ACLs on switches under this deployment |

### `system_sdwan_delete_ovn_acl`

Delete an OVN ACL. Effect: ACL row destroyed and excluded from next OVN compile; northbound database reapplies on next reconcile.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `acl_id` | string | Yes | Sdwan::OvnAcl id |

### `system_sdwan_delete_ovn_logical_switch`

Delete an OVN logical switch. Cascades attached logical switch ports and ACLs scoped to the switch.

- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

### `system_sdwan_delete_ovn_deployment`

Decommission an OVN deployment. Cascades logical switches, ports, and ACLs under it. Irreversible.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: sdwan.networks.read

### `system_sdwan_delete_ipfix_collector`

Delete an IPFIX collector. Next topology compile drops the ipfix: block from per-host payloads.

### `system_provision_docker_runtime`

Tear down a managed Docker daemon: destroy the Devops::DockerHost row and purge its TLS material from Vault. The NodeInstance and its docker-engine module assignment are untouched — operator must unassign the module separately if they want the agent to stop dockerd.

### `platform_provisioning_capture_brief`

Translate a natural-language utterance into a structured Project Brief. When mission_id is omitted, creates a new infrastructure mission bound to the system_provisioning template. When mission_id is provided, treats the utterance as a clarification and merges fields onto the existing brief. Returns the brief plus the list of fields still missing for plan composition.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: none

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | No | Existing infrastructure mission ID — omit to create a new one |
| `natural_language` | string | Yes | Operator's natural-language description of what they want to provision |
| `prior_brief` | object | No | Optional existing brief to merge new fields onto (auto-loaded from mission.configuration['brief'] when mission_id is given) |

### `platform_provisioning_compose_plan`

Run the LLM goal-decomposition kernel against the mission's brief and produce a persisted Ai::GoalPlan whose steps are rewritten into provisioning_skill shape. Returns the DAG plus M1 enrichments: cost_estimate (CostEstimatorService), topology_preview (TopologyRendererService), and risk (RiskScorerService).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: none

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | Infrastructure mission ID |

### `platform_provisioning_approve_plan`

Operator decision on a composed plan. decision='approved' advances the mission past the review_plan gate; 'rejected' sends it back to compose_plan via rejection_mappings; 'modified' applies inline edits to the plan steps before approving. The optional approval_request_id field in the response is reserved for M1 when this routes through the formal approval pipeline.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: none

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `plan_id` | string | Yes | Ai::GoalPlan ID returned by compose_plan |
| `decision` | string | Yes | One of: approved, rejected, modified |
| `modifications` | object | No | Optional plan-step edits to apply when decision='modified' (shape: { steps: [{ step_number: Int, skill: String }] }) |

### `platform_provisioning_status`

Snapshot of provisioning progress: mission phase, currently-executing step number, and step-number lists by status (completed, pending, failed). For live streaming subscribe to MissionChannel rather than polling this.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: none

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | Infrastructure mission ID |

### `platform_provisioning_adapt`

M0 stub — adaptation engine ships with the ProjectSloSensor reconciler in M2. Returns { todo: 'M2', adaptation_plan: nil } today; will accept a proposed_change (scale_horizontal, cost_control, schema_change, etc.) and return a remediation plan in M2.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: none

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | Infrastructure mission ID |
| `proposed_change` | object | No | Optional shape of the adaptation; ignored in M0 |

Optionally also mints a Gitea PAT and sets it as PLATFORM_READ_TOKEN for the parent platform checkout step. Idempotent: re-running with the same label rotates secrets + token.

| `files_changed` | array | No | Paths touched by this task |

### `data_source_invalidate_cache`

Invalidate cached responses via Ai::DataSources::ResponseCacheService. With a tag, clears every entry under that surrogate key (ResponseCacheService.invalidate_by_tag). Otherwise clears by scope: data_source + endpoint_id clears that endpoint's variants, data_source alone clears all of the source's entries. Requires ai.data_sources.update (or .manage).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | No | Data source UUID or slug (required unless tag is given) |
| `endpoint_id` | string | No | Endpoint UUID or slug to scope the invalidation |
| `tag` | string | No | Surrogate cache tag (e.g. ds:<id>, endpoint:<id>, slug:<slug>); takes precedence over scope |

### `data_source_export`

Export a data source's CREDENTIAL-FREE config manifest via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#export (source + endpoints MINUS all secrets). The manifest carries the auth_scheme NAME and non-secret broker knobs only — never api keys, credentials, or secret auth_config values. Re-importable to recreate the source elsewhere.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | Data source UUID or slug |

### `data_source_import`

Import a CREDENTIAL-FREE config manifest into the account via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#import (create-or-update the source by slug, upsert endpoints by slug, all in one transaction). NEVER sets credentials — attach those separately after import. Requires ai.data_sources.create or .manage; agents lacking it file a proposal. Supports dry_run to preview the create/update plan without persisting.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `manifest` | object | Yes | Credential-free manifest (as produced by data_source_export) |
| `slug` | string | No | Override target source slug (clones under a new slug; name auto-deduped) |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Preview the create/update plan without persisting (default false) |

### `data_source_list_templates`

List the built-in library of reusable, credential-free data-source templates (Ai::DataSources::TemplateLibrary). Each entry is a starter manifest for a well-known or generic source: slug, name, description, category.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read
- **Parameters**: none

### `data_source_install_template`

Install a library template by slug into the account via Ai::DataSources::TemplateLibrary.install (materializes the template's credential-free manifest through ConfigPortabilityService#import). NEVER sets credentials — attach those afterward if the source requires auth. Requires ai.data_sources.create or .manage; agents lacking it file a proposal.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `template_slug` | string | Yes | Catalog slug of the template to install (see data_source_list_templates) |

### `data_source_config_versions`

List a data source's append-only config-version history (Ai::DataSourceConfigVersion), latest first: version number, created_by_type (auto|manual|rollback), note, and created_at. Each row is a credential-free manifest snapshot captured by snapshot!/rollback.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | Data source UUID or slug |

### `data_source_rollback_config`

Roll a data source's config back to a prior version via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#rollback! (captures the current state as a new 'rollback' snapshot first, then replays the historical manifest — credentials are never touched). Requires ai.data_sources.manage; agents lacking it file a proposal.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | Data source UUID or slug |
| `version` | integer | Yes | Config version NUMBER to restore |

### `data_source_reconcile`

DETERMINISTIC multi-source merge: governed-fetch every target (Ai::DataSources::QueryService) INDEPENDENTLY, collect each successful FetchEnvelope's records, then collapse them into one list by EXACT canonical-key match via Ai::DataSources::ReconciliationService (strategy first_wins|last_wins|merge). No cross-source SQL/join, no fuzzy entity resolution — exact key merge only. Requires ai.data_sources.query (it fetches). Returns the merged records plus per-source status.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `targets` | array | Yes | Targets to fetch + merge; each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } |
| `key` | string | Yes | Canonical key field name shared across the sources |
| `strategy` | string | No | Merge strategy: first_wins|last_wins|merge (default last_wins) |
| `params` | object | No | Query params forwarded to EVERY target fetch |

### `data_source_failover_query`

Ordered FAILOVER across equivalent targets via Ai::DataSources::FailoverService#query: try each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } IN ORDER (primary first) through the full governed QueryService pipeline and return the FIRST success; if all fail, return the last failure envelope. Requires ai.data_sources.query. Returns the winning FetchEnvelope with failover provenance (failover_used/failover_attempts/failover_source).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `targets` | array | Yes | Ordered targets (primary first); each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } |
| `params` | object | No | Query params forwarded to every attempt |

### `data_source_replay`

Forensic, side-effect-free REPLAY of a recorded fetch via Ai::DataSources::ReplayService#replay: reconstruct a FetchEnvelope-shaped view from the redacted ai_data_source_queries audit row WITHOUT any network call, signing, or credential resolution. The cached body (when still present and the original params are supplied) is RE-MASKED for the current requester. Requires ai.data_sources.read.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `query_id` | string | No | ai_data_source_queries row UUID to replay |
| `correlation_id` | string | No | Fetch correlation id to replay |
| `params` | object | No | Original request params — supplied ONLY to recover the cached (re-masked) body |

### `data_source_ingest_to_kb`

RAG ingestion bridge: governed-fetch a source+endpoint (Ai::DataSources::QueryService) then pipe the canonical records into a knowledge base as embedded Ai::Document rows via Ai::DataSources::RagIngestionService#ingest (source_type "api", incremental re-embed dedup by record key). Requires ai.data_sources.manage (it writes documents/embeddings); agents lacking it file a proposal. Returns the ingest counts (ingested/updated/skipped/capped/errors).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | Data source UUID or slug to fetch from |
| `endpoint_id` | string | Yes | Endpoint UUID or slug to fetch |
| `knowledge_base_id` | string | Yes | Target knowledge base UUID |
| `key` | string | No | Canonical record-key field for incremental re-embed dedup (optional) |
| `params` | object | No | Query/path/body parameters for the fetch |

### `trading_create_training_session`

Create a new AI training session. Defaults to continuous mode. All params can be passed at top level or nested under 'config'.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::TradingSimulationTool`
- **Permission**: trading.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `strategy_id` | string | No | Strategy ID or name (optional) |
| `config` | object | No | Training session configuration (alternative: pass params at top level) |
| `name` | string | No | Session name |
| `mode` | string | No | Session mode: 'continuous' (default) or 'fixed_ticks' |
| `strategy_types` | array | No | Strategy types to run |
| `market_count` | integer | No | Number of markets to discover |
| `tick_count` | integer | No | Number of ticks to run (only for fixed_ticks mode) |
| `tick_interval` | integer | No | Seconds between ticks |
| `initial_balance` | number | No | Starting balance in USD |
| `venue_slug` | string | No | Trading venue slug (e.g. 'kalshi') |
| `risk_tier` | string | No | Risk tier (low/medium/high) |
| `include_classic` | boolean | No | Deprecated — use strategy_types array to specify all desired types |
| `bypass_suppression` | boolean | No | Bypass intelligence suppression — allow strategies that would normally be blocked by poor historical performance |
| `use_performance_sizing` | boolean | No | Enable performance-based position sizing (scales size by win rate) |
| `probability_min` | number | No | Min probability filter for market selection |
| `probability_max` | number | No | Max probability filter for market selection |
| `min_volume_24h` | number | No | Min 24h volume filter |
| `compounding_enabled` | boolean | No | Enable profit compounding |
| `compounding_threshold_pct` | number | No | P&L threshold % to trigger compounding |
| `compounding_reinvest_pct` | integer | No | Percentage of profits to reinvest (0-100) |
| `confidence_threshold` | number | No | Minimum confidence score to enter positions |
| `rebalance_enabled` | boolean | No | Enable mid-session capital rebalancing (shifts capital from losers to winners) |
| `rebalance_interval_ticks` | integer | No | Rebalance every N ticks (default: 5) |
| `rebalance_smoothing_factor` | number | No | 0.0=no change, 1.0=full redistribution (default: 0.5) |
| `rebalance_min_ticks` | integer | No | Minimum ticks before first rebalance (default: 3) |
| `rebalance_decommission_enabled` | boolean | No | Allow mid-session strategy decommission for severe underperformers (default: true) |
| `include_series` | array | No | Series ticker prefixes to scope discovery (e.g. ['KXFED', 'KXBTC']). Drastically speeds up discovery by skipping irrelevant series. |
| `exclude_series` | array | No | Series ticker prefixes to exclude from discovery |
| `scheduled_for` | string | No | ISO8601 datetime to schedule session for future start (sets status to 'scheduled'). Overseer auto-starts when time arrives. |
| `duration_minutes` | integer | No | Session duration in minutes for continuous mode. Sets ends_at relative to start time (or scheduled_for). Overseer auto-completes when expired. Omit for indefinite. |
| `profit_hunter_enabled` | boolean | No | Enable adaptive profit hunting — auto-prunes zero-performers, rotates dead markets, deploys reserve capital on new strategy/market combos |
| `profit_hunter_reserve_pct` | number | No | Fraction of capital held in reserve for hunting (default: 0.15 = 15%) |
| `profit_hunter_fast_prune_ticks` | integer | No | Prune strategies after N consecutive zero-result ticks (default: 3) |
| `profit_hunter_hunt_interval` | integer | No | Run hunting loop every N ticks (default: 5) |
| `profit_hunter_max_experiments` | integer | No | Max concurrent experimental strategies from hunting (default: 3) |
| `profit_hunter_llm_budget_usd` | number | No | Cap LLM spend on exploration — prefers zero-LLM strategy types (default: 2.0) |

### `trading_seed_profit_formula`

Seed the Profit Formula portfolio — tuned parameters for 9 zero-LLM-cost strategies (arbitrage, tail_end_yield, combinatorial_arbitrage, longshot_fading, prediction_market_making, mean_reversion, momentum, cross_platform_arbitrage, spot_lag_arbitrage). Overwrites global defaults with empirically-optimized values from 136 training runs. Also sets venue-specific overrides for Polymarket (zero fees) and Kalshi.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::TradingSimulationTool`
- **Permission**: trading.manage
- **Parameters**: none

| `slug` | string | No | Polymarket event slug (alternative to ticker for PM) |
| `interval` | string | No | Candle interval (default: '1h') |
| `limit` | integer | No | Max pairs to import from registry (default: 50) |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `strategy_type` | string | Yes | Strategy type to sweep (e.g. 'prediction_market_making') |

| `sweep_id` | string | No | Existing sweep ID to collect results (skip creation) |
| `method` | string | No | Combination method: 'grid' (default) or 'lhs' |
| `max_combos` | integer | No | Max parameter combinations (default: 64) |
| `tick_count` | integer | No | Ticks per backtest (default: 50) |
| `initial_balance` | number | No | Starting balance (default: 10000) |
| `promote_best` | boolean | No | Auto-promote best params to global defaults if profitable |

### `code_context_tree`

Get an AST-based structural tree of the codebase with file headers and symbol ranges. Dynamic pruning by depth.

- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | No | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `base_path` | string | No | Filesystem path to codebase root |
| `path` | string | No | Subdirectory to scan (default: root) |
| `max_depth` | integer | No | Maximum tree depth (default 3) |
| `include_symbols` | boolean | No | Include parsed symbols (default true) |

### `code_file_skeleton`

Get function signatures, class methods, and type definitions for a file — no function bodies, just the structure with line ranges.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeDiscoveryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | No | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `base_path` | string | No | Filesystem path to codebase root |
| `file_path` | string | Yes | File path relative to codebase root |

Semantic search over code symbols using embeddings. Finds code by meaning, not just name.

- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `query` | string | Yes | Search query |
| `entity_types` | array | No | Filter by entity types (class, method, function, etc.) |
| `top_k` | integer | No | Max results (default 10) |

Search for identifiers (functions, classes, variables) by name or semantic meaning with usage counts.

|-----------|------|----------|-------------|

| `query` | string | Yes | Identifier name or description |

Browse the codebase by meaning using semantic clustering. Groups related files and symbols into labeled clusters.

| `query` | string | No | Optional focus query to filter clusters |
| `cluster_id` | integer | No | Specific cluster ID to inspect |

Obsidian-style feature navigation from markdown files with [[wikilinks]]. Discovers documentation structure and orphan files.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|

| `base_path` | string | No | Filesystem path to codebase root |

Trace every file and line where a symbol is imported or used. Shows the impact radius of changing a function, class, or module.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `symbol_name` | string | No | Symbol name (qualified or simple) |
| `node_id` | string | No | Knowledge graph node ID |
| `max_depth` | integer | No | Maximum traversal depth (default 3, max 5) |

Run native linters and compilers (RuboCop, TypeScript, ESLint). Returns structured diagnostics with file, line, severity, and message.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|

| `base_path` | string | No | Filesystem path to codebase root |

### `code_index_status`

Show codebase indexing statistics: files indexed, symbols extracted, last indexed timestamp, stale files count.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeAnalysisTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |

### `code_dead_code`

Detect dead code via language-native analyzers (ts-prune for TS, debride for Ruby) + grep verification + AI triage. Async — dispatched to the worker; the categorized result (real_dead / public_api / dynamic_dispatch / test_only / uncertain) is written to shared memory, retrieve via read_shared_memory.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeAnalysisTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `languages` | array | No | Subset of [typescript, ruby] (default: both) |
| `triage` | boolean | No | Run LLM triage of verified candidates (default: true) |
| `model` | string | No | Override the triage LLM model |

### `code_find_duplicates`

Detect copy-paste code clones via jscpd (token-based) + AI triage. Async — dispatched to the worker; the categorized result (extract_candidate / acceptable / generated / coincidental, with suggested actions) is written to shared memory, retrieve via read_shared_memory.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeAnalysisTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `scope_paths` | array | No | Subdirs to scan (default: frontend/src, server/app, worker/app) |
| `min_tokens` | integer | No | Clone size floor in tokens (default: 50) |
| `triage` | boolean | No | Run LLM triage of clone groups (default: true) |
| `model` | string | No | Override the triage LLM model |

### `code_analyze_section`

Run focused dead code + duplicate analysis on a codebase section. Omit section to auto-discover sections. Use scope_path to limit discovery to a subtree.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeAnalysisTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `section` | string | No | Section path to analyze (e.g. 'server/app/models', 'frontend/src/features'). Omit to list available sections. |
| `scope_path` | string | No | Limit section discovery to a subtree (e.g. 'server/app/services', 'frontend/src') |
| `dead_code` | boolean | No | Run dead code detection (default: true) |
| `duplicates` | boolean | No | Run duplicate detection (default: true) |
| `duplicate_threshold` | number | No | Similarity threshold for duplicates (default: 0.92) |
| `min_dead_score` | number | No | Minimum deadness score (default: 0.5) |

### `code_upsert_node`

Create or update a code-aware knowledge graph node. Auto-generates embeddings for semantic search.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `name` | string | Yes | Qualified node name (e.g. 'User#full_name') |
| `entity_type` | string | Yes | Entity type: file, directory, class, module, method, function, variable, type_definition, interface, constant |
| `file_path` | string | No | File path relative to codebase root |
| `line_range` | string | No | Line range (e.g. '10-25') |
| `description` | string | No | Human-readable description |
| `properties` | object | No | Additional metadata |

### `code_create_relation`

Create a typed edge between two code nodes (e.g. imports, calls, inherits).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `source_node_id` | string | Yes | Source node ID |
| `target_node_id` | string | Yes | Target node ID |
| `relation_type` | string | Yes | Relation type: imports, calls, defines, inherits, implements, contains, related_to, depends_on, uses |
| `weight` | number | No | Edge weight 0-1 (default 1.0) |
| `properties` | object | No | Edge metadata |

### `code_search_graph`

Search the code graph with optional multi-hop traversal. Combines name matching with graph expansion.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `query` | string | Yes | Search query |
| `entity_types` | array | No | Filter by entity types |
| `max_depth` | integer | No | Graph traversal depth (default 2) |
| `top_k` | integer | No | Max results (default 10) |

### `code_prune_stale`

Find and remove/archive code nodes for files that no longer exist on disk (async — dispatched to the worker; result written to shared memory, retrieve via read_shared_memory). Use dry_run to preview.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | Preview without executing (default true) |

### `code_bulk_index`

Trigger codebase indexing (async — dispatched to the worker; returns immediately). Parses source files, creates knowledge graph nodes/edges, and generates embeddings. Track progress with code_index_status.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | No | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `base_path` | string | No | Filesystem path to codebase root |
| `path` | string | No | Subdirectory to index (default: entire codebase) |
| `incremental` | boolean | No | Only re-index changed files (default true) |

## Conversations & Workspaces

### `send_message`

Send a message to any conversation (workspace or agent). The conversation's agent will auto-respond (async for regular agents, sync for concierge). Include @mentions to notify specific agents in workspaces.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | Conversation ID (workspace or agent) |
| `message` | string | Yes | Message content (include @AgentName to mention) |
| `mentions` | array | No | Structured agent mentions [{"id": "...", "name": "..."}] |

### `send_concierge_message`

Send a message to the Powernode concierge and get an AI response. Creates or reuses an active concierge conversation.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `message` | string | Yes | Message to send to the concierge |

### `confirm_concierge_action`

Confirm a pending concierge action (create_mission, delegate_to_team, code_review, deploy).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | Conversation ID containing the pending action |
| `action_type` | string | Yes | Action type: create_mission, delegate_to_team, code_review, deploy |
| `action_params` | object | No | Optional parameters (overrides original params) |

### `list_messages`

Retrieve messages from any conversation (workspace or agent)

| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | Conversation UUID or conversation_id |

### `tag_conversation`

Set, add, or remove tags on a conversation. Pass `tags:` to replace, `add_tag:` to append, or `remove_tag:` to remove.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | Conversation UUID or conversation_id |
| `tags` | array | No | Replace the conversation's tag list with this array |
| `add_tag` | string | No | Append a single tag (idempotent — won't dup) |
| `remove_tag` | string | No | Remove a single tag |
